survey: A round-bellied cauldron of green, bubbling liquid stands on a tiled floor in a room with a pink wall at the back. The camera is a little above the rim. The rim is a wide, fairly flat ellipse, so we see the liquid surface from above, and the bubbles sit flat on that surface. Two ring handles hang from square lugs at the left and right edges of the belly. The rings face the camera, which matches rings hanging in the plane that runs outward from the pot's centre, so they are consistent. The pot stands on three short legs. The front-left leg is nearest the viewer and lowest on the image. The right leg is set further back, sitting higher and drawn smaller, and the third leg is hidden behind the pot. The bottoms of the feet are rounder ellipses than the rim, which is correct because they are further below the eye level. Crossed sticks with a glowing fire sit under the belly, also seen slightly from above. The floor-tile lines run diagonally and shrink into the distance. The cauldron is turned at an angle to the tile grid, which is allowed, and its feet sit flat on the floor plane at the angle the floor is drawn. The rim, feet, fire and floor all agree on one slightly-high viewpoint.
